title: Fall Protection Inspection Checklist (OSHA 29 CFR 1926.501)
subtitle: Use when a work area at height is set up, after any change to edges, openings or roof work, and on routine site walks.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A; use N/A only when that work or condition is not on site.
For each Defect, keep workers away from the exposure until it is corrected, then record the fix, who made it and the date.
The manufacturer's instructions for each system and your site rules may add checks; 1926.502 sets the criteria the systems must meet.

sections.title: Surfaces, edges and openings
items: The employer has determined the surface can support employees safely; nobody works on a surface not yet confirmed as strong enough.
Guardrails, nets and arrest equipment on site match the 1926.502 criteria for that type of system.
Every side or edge with a drop of 6 ft or more has a guardrail or safety net, or each exposed worker uses a PFAS.
Guardrail or PFAS where workers could fall at least 6 ft; anyone leaning through an opening with the guardrail, chain or gate removed is protected by a PFAS.
Guardrail systems along each ramp, runway or walkway where the fall to the level below is at least 6 ft.
Openings whose outside bottom edge is 6 ft or higher above lower levels and whose inside bottom edge is under 39 in above the working surface are guarded by guardrail, net or PFAS.
Any surface 6 ft or higher not covered by another item has a guardrail, net or PFAS.

sections.title: Holes, excavations and dangerous equipment
items: Each hole or skylight more than 6 ft above a lower level is covered or guardrailed, or workers near it use a PFAS.
Covers are in place over holes and skylights where workers could trip in or step into or through them.
Covers stop objects falling through holes and skylights onto workers.
Excavations 6 ft deep or more that are hidden by plant growth or another visual barrier have guardrails, fences or barricades at the edge.
Wells, pits, shafts and similar excavations 6 ft or deeper have guardrails, fences, barricades or covers.
Workers less than 6 ft above dangerous equipment are kept from falling into or onto it by guardrails or equipment guards.
Dangerous equipment at 6 ft or more
Workers 6 ft or more above dangerous equipment are protected by guardrails, a PFAS or safety nets.

sections.title: Roofs, leading edges and specific trades
items: Roofers have guardrails, nets, a PFAS, or a warning line system combined with a guardrail, net, PFAS or safety monitor.
A safety monitor working without warning lines is used only on low-slope roofs 50 ft (15.25 m) wide or less.
Guardrail systems with toeboards, safety nets or PFAS protect everyone on the steep roof.

Workers building a leading edge use guardrails, nets or a PFAS, or a 1926.502(k) fall protection plan is in place and followed after the employer has shown those systems are infeasible or more hazardous.

Workers on a surface where leading edges are being built, but not doing that work, have PFAS, nets or guardrails; a control line replaces the guardrail along the edge parallel to the leading edge only where the leading edge crew already works inside its own controlled access zone.
Workers erecting or grouting precast members have guardrails, nets or PFAS, or the 1926.502(k) plan exception applies.

Residential crews working at height have guardrails, a safety net or a PFAS, an alternative allowed by another paragraph (b) provision, or a 1926.502(k) plan where the employer has demonstrated infeasibility or a greater hazard.
Workers on the face of formwork or reinforcing steel use a PFAS, safety net or positioning device system.
Bricklayers have a PFAS, guardrails or a safety net, or work within the controlled access zone.
Anyone reaching more than 10 in (25 cm) below the surface they stand on is protected by a guardrail system, a net or a PFAS.

sections.title: Falling objects
items: Every worker in a falling-object zone wears a hard hat, and at least one of items D2 to D4 is in place.
If used, toeboards, screens or guardrails stop objects dropping from the levels above.
If chosen, a canopy covers the work area below and loose material is kept back from the upper edge so it cannot go over if knocked.
Alternatively, the area where objects could land is barricaded, entry is prohibited, and material is stored back from the edge so it cannot go over if displaced.

references: 29 CFR 1926.501: Duty to have fall protection (Part 1926, Subpart M: Fall Protection)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
